<a id="what-a-cut-loses-for-every-schedule-of-couplings--截断所失任意耦合时程"></a>
# What a cut loses, for every schedule of couplings

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`what-a-cut-loses` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](what-a-cut-loses.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> For every schedule of couplings, a cut at order j loses exactly what j + 1 responses carry, where a longer chain in time order arrives; once the schedule settles, a finite order is exact exactly where no loop of continuing couplings lies upstream, the only way past every polynomial.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. One response carries to a condition what the strengths make of given levels, with no starting gap and no gap of the part; j responses carry in turn. Giving and carrying are additive in the levels read, so the carried amount is the orders below j plus what j responses in turn carry from it: a cut at order j loses exactly what j + 1 responses carry. The loss does not grow as the order rises. (`Becoming.Remainder.mul_pos_nat`, `Becoming.Remainder.add_left_cancel_nat`, `Becoming.Remainder.le_of_add_le_add_left_nat`, `Becoming.responded`, `Becoming.responses`, `Becoming.responded_zero`, `Becoming.responded_succ`, `Becoming.carriedGive_add`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_add`, `Becoming.carried_eq_orderBelow_add`, `Becoming.carried_eq_carriedWithin_add`, `Becoming.responses_antitone`)
2. With the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D and the strengths into each condition summing to at most M at each step, what a cut loses is at most the bound of Becoming.Loops, whatever the schedule of couplings; the self-loop loses exactly that bound. (`Becoming.responses_le_missBound`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.responses_eq`)
3. One response carries something to c by step t exactly where, at an earlier step, a positive level is coupled into c. A gap is conveyed through j responses or more where a route in time reaches a condition and j couplings carry it on, each reading a level the one before had reached; the orders below j miss something at c at step t exactly where a gap is so conveyed there. (`Becoming.CouplesAt`, `Becoming.couples_iff_couplesAt`, `Becoming.responded_pos_iff`, `Becoming.ConveyedThrough`, `Becoming.responses_pos_iff`, `Becoming.orderBelow_lt_iff`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_lt_iff`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_eq_iff`)
4. A chain of j couplings in time order ends at c by step t, each reading a level the one before had reached; it needs j steps, and without time it is a chain of couplings. Order j is exact at c at step t from every start exactly where no such chain of j + 1 couplings ends there; a finite order is exact at c at every step from every start exactly where those chains are bounded, one order then serving every start. (`Becoming.CoupledIntoBy`, `Becoming.ConveyedThrough.coupledIntoBy`, `Becoming.conveyed_ones`, `Becoming.CoupledIntoBy.conveyedThrough_ones`, `Becoming.CoupledIntoBy.later`, `Becoming.CoupledIntoBy.shorten`, `Becoming.CoupledIntoBy.le_steps`, `Becoming.CoupledIntoBy.coupledInto`, `Becoming.exact_every_start_iff`, `Becoming.finite_order_iff_bounded`, `Becoming.finite_order_uniform_iff`)
5. A coupling recurs where it reads levels at steps as late as one likes. Where a gap reaches a loop of recurring couplings, and recurring couplings lead on to c, each time around adds the loop's length to the responses, so every order misses something at c and the chains in time order into c are unbounded. Where no coupling reads a level from step N on, order N is exact everywhere from every start. (`Becoming.CouplingRecurs`, `Becoming.CouplesAlways.recurs`, `Becoming.Conveyed.later`, `Becoming.ConveyedThrough.later`, `Becoming.conveyedThrough_along`, `Becoming.conveyedThrough_around`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_lt_of_recurring_loop`, `Becoming.unbounded_of_recurring_loop`, `Becoming.exact_of_reading_before`)
6. Each coupling reads a listed condition, so a chain one longer than the list passes a loop, with no listing of every condition; where no loop lies upstream of c, a chain in time order into c has at most as many couplings as there are conditions (one fewer with every condition listed). Couplings holding at every step recur, so there the chains are bounded exactly where no loop lies upstream. (`Becoming.loop_of_coupledInto_succ`, `Becoming.no_chain_of_no_loop`, `Becoming.no_chain_of_no_loop_listed`, `Becoming.bounded_iff_no_loop`)
7. The strengths from step N on drop every reading of a level before N. A coupling recurs exactly where it couples from every step on; the last j of a chain in time order of N + j couplings couple from N on. The schedule has settled by step N where every coupling from N on recurs; then, for any list of conditions, a finite order is exact at c from every start exactly where no loop of those couplings lies upstream. (`Becoming.strengthsFrom`, `Becoming.couplesAt_strengthsFrom`, `Becoming.couples_strengthsFrom_iff`, `Becoming.couplingRecurs_iff`, `Becoming.CoupledIntoBy.tail`, `Becoming.SettledFrom`, `Becoming.settledFrom_zero_of_always`, `Becoming.bounded_iff_no_loop_from`, `Becoming.finite_order_iff_no_loop_from`)
8. Whatever the schedule, where no loop of the couplings from some step N on lies upstream of c, a chain in time order into c has at most N plus the number of conditions couplings, and the carried amount, the most difference that can arrive, is at most D times a polynomial in the steps of that degree: faster than every polynomial only through a loop of the couplings that go on. (`Becoming.no_chain_of_no_loop_from`, `Becoming.carried_le_polynomial_from`)
9. The loop of Loops.Once reads the first step only: it has no chain of two couplings in time order, nothing couples from the second step on, and its schedule has settled. The results of Becoming.Loops on exactness are instances: order j is exact up to step j; no loop upstream suffices; the equivalence where couplings hold at every step, without its listing; order one is exact for the loop coupled once. (`Becoming.Loops.Once.reads_first`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.no_chain_of_two`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.none_from_one`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.settled`, `Becoming.Remainder.carriedWithin_exact`, `Becoming.Remainder.carriedWithin_exact_of_no_loop`, `Becoming.Remainder.finite_order_iff_no_loop`, `Becoming.Remainder.Once.exact`)
10. With each condition listed once: for every law of what has stood with these strengths and every two balanced flows of it, every gap at c at step T, from every start, is at most what order j carries exactly where no chain of j + 1 couplings in time order ends there. (`Becoming.gap_within_order_iff`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. The coupling strengths (the k of RespondsWithin) are supplied bounds; the schedule of couplings is arbitrary, and so is the list of conditions, every condition being listed only where a theorem writes every.
- In the bounds, the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D and the strengths into each condition at most M at each step; in the settled equivalences, the schedule settled by step N (SettledFrom), written in as a hypothesis.
- In the theorem for every law, each condition listed once (Distinct), with decided equality of conditions used only in its proof, through most_difference_arrives.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That every schedule settles at some step: classically true for finitely many conditions, but whether a coupling recurs is not decided here, and the core assumes no excluded middle.
- A loop upstream does not imply that no finite order is exact: where the loop couples at the first step only, no chain of two couplings in time order arrives. Witness: `Becoming.Loops.Once.no_chain_of_two`.
- That every loop of recurring couplings makes the most difference that can arrive run away, or how fast: every finite order being inexact is no rate.
- Which strengths and schedule a given law has; real amounts, continuous time, and laws reading infinitely many conditions at a step.
- **Counterexample:** The loop coupled once: one condition, whose one formation returns its level to it at the first step only; the loop lies upstream, yet chains in time order have at most one coupling, so order one is exact from every start: the loops that matter are those of the couplings that go on. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Loops.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Ren, 12 October 2026, on the loops: “how how accurate can we do that uh what is the limitation do we have losses”, with the goal “move towards 100%”; on 16 October, deciding the readings of Becoming.Loops, Ren left couplings at only some steps open. This result answers the first item of how-a-carried-difference-grows' next_delta. Readings (the AI's, taken by Ren on 18 October 2026, DELEGATED-CHOICES D43): the exact remainder is the remainder of the expansion Ren took as the same structural kind as the sum over histories, in the form of a Neumann series's remainder, its responses in time order as in the Dyson series; the loss is the cut's, not the theory's. What decides a cut's loss is the time order of the couplings: the loops that matter are those of the couplings that go on, and a loop whose couplings stop is passing. The most difference that can arrive outgrows every polynomial only through a loop of the couplings that go on, and not through every such loop, since one that recurs rarely stays polynomial (Frequency.Sparse.polynomial, how-often-couplings-act). The mathematics is standard: the Neumann, Dyson or Peano–Baker remainder of a linear time-varying comparison system, nilpotent exactly where the time-respecting paths are bounded.

  - Output: A sequence held by a list revisits within the length of the list.

  - Preserved conditions: The terms of the sequence are listed: each coupling reads a listed condition. [Recurrence.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Recurrence.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [losses-of-the-sum-over-histories](losses-of-the-sum-over-histories.md). The other integration Ren took as the same structural kind: there a truncation of the sum over histories misses exactly what it drops; here a cut at order j loses exactly what more responses carry. orders-as-a-sum-over-histories joins the two: a cut at order j is a truncation of the sum over histories at horizon j + 1.
- related, not a proved adapter: [orders-as-a-sum-over-histories](orders-as-a-sum-over-histories.md). A cut is a horizon: a cut at order j is the truncation at horizon j + 1 of the sum over routes back in time, so what a cut loses is what that truncation of the sum over histories drops.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-often-couplings-act](how-often-couplings-act.md). Answers the first two items of its next step: every schedule settling is exactly the dichotomy RecursOrStops, which gives the limited principle of omniscience; a loop of recurring couplings need not run away, runs away where its returns are frequent, and the rate counts the steps at which couplings act.
